answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by granting one active identity per unique normalized postal address. Enrollment mails a one-time code to that address; the ledger hashes the normalized string and rejects a second registration at the same string, so the code cannot wander to another account at that address. A juniper lane address and a cedar court address are distinct strings, each granting exactly one slot. The scarce resource is addresses, not humans; each extra identity needs another address costing C per epoch, so n identities yield n(R-C), deterring only while reward R<C.
